label: Person
name: Konrad Witz
summary:
Konrad Witz was a renowned German and Swiss painter active mainly in Basel during the Late Gothic period. He is best known for his intricate and detailed frescoes in the St. George's Church, which showcase his mastery of color and composition. Witz's work had a lasting impact on the development of religious art in Switzerland and beyond.

 Born into a family of modest means, Witz received a traditional apprenticeship in painting at a young age. He quickly established himself as one of the leading artists of his time, producing works that blended Byzantine and Gothic styles. In 1427, he married Elisabeth von Habsburg, a member of the powerful Habsburg dynasty.

 Despite facing financial difficulties and personal turmoil, Witz continued to produce remarkable works until his death in 1445 at the age of 99. His legacy as one of the greatest painters of the Late Gothic period endures to this day.

 As an artist who 'participated in' the artistic movements of the time, Konrad Witz was a key figure in the development of the International Gothic style, which emphasized elegance and refinement. His frescoes in St. George's Church remain some of the most celebrated examples of Late Gothic art.
